title: With Thy Pure Dews and Rains
description: With Thy Pure Dews and Rains in Tonic Solfa to DORT, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Pierpont wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 798 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Prayer for the Abolition of Slavery”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sixes and Fours (6.6.4.6.6.6.4), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to DORT; any other Sixes and Fours tune fits them as well.
underlay: With thy pure dews and rains, Wash out, O God! the stains From A-fric's shore; And while her palm trees bud, Let not her chil-dren's blood, With her broad Ni-ger's flood, Be min-gled more.

lines: With thy pure dews and rains,
Wash out, O God! the stains
And while her palm trees bud,
Hear'st thou, O God! those chains,
Those who these chains have worn,
Lord! wilt thou not, at last,
Save those of love, which brings
Back — to the King of kings, —

licence: Public domain: John Pierpont died in 1866.
credits: Words by John Pierpont (1785–1866), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to DORT by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
